meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: A label and the control it describes
questions.learningObjective: Identify how a label associates with a control
questions.stem: A debate team uses a label with a for attribute matching an input id.

options.text: The label is programmatically associated with the control
The label only styles the input
The label submits the form automatically

questions.explanation: The for attribute links the label to the control by id. This association aids accessibility and click targeting.

questions.topic: Where a required field is enforced
questions.stem: A debate form marks an input as required.

options.text: Validation occurs only on the server
The browser blocks submission until the field is filled
The field is optional despite the attribute

questions.explanation: The required attribute triggers client-side validation before submission. Server validation should still be added separately.

questions.topic: Tabs and spaces in source and in a preserved listing
questions.learningObjective: Predict rendered output of tabs in normal flow
questions.stem: A paragraph contains tab characters between words in a debate transcript.

options.text: Tabs render as fixed tab stops like in a terminal
Tabs are removed entirely with no gap
Tabs collapse to a single space in normal flow

questions.explanation: In normal flow, tab characters collapse to a single space like other white space. Terminal tab stops do not apply to HTML.

questions.topic: Why the initial box-sizing surprises people
questions.stem: A developer expects width 200px to include padding and border.

answer.exemplar: The default content-box excludes padding and border from the declared width, so the rendered box is wider than expected; border-box would include them.

questions.explanation: Content-box counts only content in the width. Padding and border add outside, causing the surprise.

questions.topic: Which flex property works along the line and which across it
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish main-axis from cross-axis flex properties
questions.stem: A debate layout uses flexbox with justify-content and align-items.

options.text: justify-content works along the line and align-items across it
justify-content works across the line and align-items along it

questions.explanation: justify-content distributes space along the main axis, while align-items aligns along the cross axis. Swapping them is a common mistake.
questions.hint: justify is main axis, align is cross.

questions.topic: What a media query changes and what it leaves alone
questions.learningObjective: Identify what a media query can change
questions.stem: A media query changes layout at a breakpoint in a debate page.

options.text: It changes CSS rules that match the condition

questions.explanation: Media queries activate CSS rules based on conditions. They do not alter HTML structure or encoding.

questions.topic: Breaking a tie between equally specific rules
questions.stem: Two rules have equal specificity in a debate stylesheet.

options.text: The first rule in source order wins
The last rule in source order wins

questions.explanation: When specificity is equal, the later rule in source order wins. The first rule does not win.
questions.hint: Last in source order wins ties.

questions.topic: Dividing a grid container between three fractional tracks
questions.learningObjective: Compute track sizes from fr units
questions.stem: A grid has three columns of 1fr each in a 300px container.
questions.explanation: Three equal 1fr tracks share the 300px container equally, giving 100px each.

questions.topic: A fixed track beside a fractional one
questions.learningObjective: Compute track sizes with a fixed and fr track
questions.stem: A grid has one 100px column and one 1fr column in a 400px container.

answer.exemplar: The fr column is 300px because the fixed column takes 100px first, leaving 300px for the fractional track.

questions.explanation: The fixed track is subtracted first, then the fr track takes the remaining space. The fr column is 300px.
questions.hint: Subtract fixed, then fr takes rest.

questions.topic: Weighted shrinking along a flex line
questions.stem: Two flex items have flex-shrink 1 and 3 in a debate layout.

options.text: Both shrink by the same amount
The item with shrink 1 shrinks more
The item with shrink 3 shrinks more
Neither shrinks because flex items never shrink

questions.explanation: Higher flex-shrink means the item gives up more space when shrinking. The item with shrink 3 shrinks more.

questions.topic: A label and the control it describes
questions.stem: A label wraps an input without a for attribute in a debate form.

options.text: There is no association without for
The input is disabled by the label

options.misconception: thinks missing for voids the label

options.text: The wrapped input is implicitly associated

questions.explanation: Wrapping an input inside a label creates an implicit association. The for attribute is not required in that case.

questions.topic: Where a required field is enforced
questions.stem: A required input is empty when the form is submitted.

options.text: The browser shows a validation message and blocks submission
The browser submits anyway and the server rejects it
The form resets to default values

questions.explanation: The required attribute prevents submission and shows a browser validation message. The server is not reached until it is valid.

questions.topic: Tabs and spaces in source and in a preserved listing
questions.stem: A pre element contains tabs and multiple spaces.

options.text: Tabs and spaces collapse like in a paragraph
Tabs become spaces and spaces vanish
Tabs and spaces are preserved as written
Only spaces are preserved, tabs are removed

questions.explanation: Preformatted text preserves white space including tabs and multiple spaces. Normal collapse does not apply.

questions.topic: Why the initial box-sizing surprises people
questions.stem: A developer is surprised that padding increases the rendered width.

answer.exemplar: The default content-box excludes padding and border from the declared width, so any padding or border adds to the outside and surprises developers expecting border-box.

questions.explanation: Content-box is the default and excludes padding and border. Developers often expect border-box behaviour instead.

questions.topic: Which flex property works along the line and which across it
questions.stem: A flex container needs items distributed along the main axis.
questions.explanation: justify-content distributes items along the main axis. align-items works on the cross axis.

questions.topic: What a media query changes and what it leaves alone
questions.learningObjective: Identify what a media query does not change
questions.stem: A media query applies at a max-width breakpoint.

options.text: It changes matching CSS rules only

questions.explanation: Media queries toggle CSS rules based on conditions. They do not change HTML, server responses, or language.

questions.topic: Breaking a tie between equally specific rules
questions.stem: Two rules have equal specificity and the same property.

options.text: The browser uses the larger value

questions.explanation: Equal specificity means source order decides, and the later rule wins. Values do not merge.

questions.topic: Dividing a grid container between three fractional tracks
questions.learningObjective: Compute track sizes from weighted fr units
questions.stem: A grid has columns 1fr, 2fr, 1fr in a 400px container.
questions.explanation: Total fr is 4, so each fr is 100px. Columns are 100px, 200px, 100px.

questions.topic: A fixed track beside a fractional one
questions.learningObjective: Compute track sizes with fixed and weighted fr
questions.stem: A grid has one 100px column and two 1fr columns in a 400px container.

answer.exemplar: The fr columns are 150px each because the fixed column takes 100px, leaving 300px split equally between two 1fr tracks.

questions.explanation: The fixed track is subtracted first, then the remaining space is shared by the fr tracks. Each fr column is 150px.

questions.topic: Weighted shrinking along a flex line
questions.stem: Two flex items have flex-shrink 0 and 2 in a debate layout.

options.text: Only the item with shrink 2 shrinks
Only the item with shrink 0 shrinks
Neither shrinks because shrink 0 blocks all

questions.explanation: The item with shrink 0 does not shrink, while the item with shrink 2 gives up space. Only the latter shrinks.

questions.topic: A label and the control it describes
questions.stem: A label is associated with an input via for and id.

options.text: Clicking the label hides the control
Clicking the label submits the form
Clicking the label focuses the control
Clicking the label disables the control

questions.explanation: Clicking an associated label focuses and activates the control. It does not submit, hide, or disable.

questions.topic: Where a required field is enforced
questions.stem: A debate form uses required on an input.

options.text: Server validation is unnecessary with required

questions.explanation: required provides client-side validation but does not replace server validation. Both layers are needed.

questions.topic: Tabs and spaces in source and in a preserved listing
questions.learningObjective: Predict rendered output of leading spaces
questions.stem: A paragraph begins with five spaces before a word.

options.text: The five spaces render as five visible gaps
The spaces collapse to a single space
The word is pushed to the next line

questions.explanation: Leading runs of white space collapse to a single space in normal flow. Source indentation does not create visible padding.

questions.topic: Why the initial box-sizing surprises people
questions.stem: A content-box element has width 120px, padding 10px, and border 2px.

answer.exemplar: The outer width is 144px because content-box adds both paddings and both borders: 120 + 10 + 10 + 2 + 2 equals 144.

questions.explanation: Content-box excludes padding and border from the declared width, so each side adds to the total. The box ends wider than 120px.
questions.hint: Add both sides of padding and border.

questions.topic: Which flex property works along the line and which across it
questions.stem: A flex container needs items aligned across the cross axis.
questions.explanation: align-items aligns items along the cross axis. justify-content works on the main axis.

questions.topic: What a media query changes and what it leaves alone
questions.stem: A media query uses min-width 600px.

options.text: It applies when the viewport is 600px or wider
It applies when the viewport is 600px or narrower

questions.explanation: min-width means the condition is true at that width and above. max-width would be the opposite.
questions.hint: min-width means at least that wide.

questions.topic: Breaking a tie between equally specific rules
questions.stem: Two rules have equal specificity and different property values.

options.text: The rule with the shorter selector wins
The rule with more properties wins
The rule appearing later in source wins

questions.explanation: Equal specificity means source order decides, and the later rule wins. Selector length and property count do not matter.

questions.topic: Dividing a grid container between three fractional tracks
questions.stem: A grid has columns 2fr, 1fr, 1fr in a 400px container.
questions.explanation: Total fr is 4, so each fr is 100px. Columns are 200px, 100px, 100px.

questions.topic: A fixed track beside a fractional one
questions.learningObjective: Compute track sizes with fixed and fr
questions.stem: A grid has one 120px column and one 1fr column in a 500px container.

answer.exemplar: The fr column is 380px because the fixed column takes 120px first, leaving 380px for the fractional track.

questions.explanation: The fixed track is subtracted first, then the fr track takes the remaining space. The fr column is 380px.
questions.hint: Subtract fixed, then fr takes rest.

questions.topic: Weighted shrinking along a flex line
questions.stem: Two flex items both have flex-shrink 1 in a debate layout.
questions.explanation: Equal flex-shrink means both give up space proportionally. They shrink equally.

questions.topic: A label and the control it describes
questions.stem: A label uses for to point to an input id in a debate form.

options.text: The for value must match the input name
The for value must match the input value
The for value must match the input type
The for value must match the input id

questions.explanation: The for attribute must match the control's id, not its name, type, or value.

questions.topic: Where a required field is enforced
questions.stem: A debate form relies only on the required attribute.
questions.explanation: Client-side required can be bypassed, so server-side validation remains necessary.

questions.topic: Tabs and spaces in source and in a preserved listing
questions.learningObjective: Predict rendered output of trailing spaces
questions.stem: A paragraph ends with several spaces after a word.

options.text: The trailing spaces render as visible gaps
The spaces become a line break
The spaces are removed but the word shifts
The spaces collapse and no trailing gap remains

questions.explanation: Trailing runs of white space collapse to a single space and do not create visible trailing gaps in normal flow.

questions.topic: Why the initial box-sizing surprises people
questions.stem: A border-box element has declared width 140px, padding 10px, and border 2px.

answer.exemplar: The content width is 116px because border-box includes padding and border in the declared width: 140 - 10 - 10 - 2 - 2 equals 116.

questions.explanation: Border-box includes padding and border in the declared width, so content is smaller than the declared width.

questions.topic: Which flex property works along the line and which across it
questions.stem: A flex container needs items to wrap onto multiple lines.
questions.explanation: flex-wrap controls whether items wrap onto multiple lines. The other properties do not wrap.

questions.topic: What a media query changes and what it leaves alone
questions.stem: A media query uses orientation landscape.

options.text: It applies only on mobile devices
It applies when height exceeds width
It applies when width exceeds height

questions.explanation: Landscape means the viewport width is greater than its height. Portrait is the opposite.

questions.topic: Breaking a tie between equally specific rules
questions.stem: Two rules have different specificity for the same property.
questions.explanation: Specificity outweighs source order. The more specific rule wins regardless of position.

questions.topic: Dividing a grid container between three fractional tracks
questions.stem: A grid has columns 3fr, 1fr, 2fr in a 600px container.
questions.explanation: Total fr is 6, so each fr is 100px. Columns are 300px, 100px, 200px.

questions.topic: A fixed track beside a fractional one
questions.learningObjective: Compute track sizes with fixed and multiple fr
questions.stem: A grid has one 80px column and two 1fr columns in a 380px container.

answer.exemplar: The fr columns are 150px each because the fixed column takes 80px, leaving 300px split equally between two 1fr tracks.

questions.explanation: The fixed track is subtracted first, then the remaining space is shared by the fr tracks. Each fr column is 150px.

questions.topic: Weighted shrinking along a flex line
questions.learningObjective: Predict shrinking with high and low weights
questions.stem: Two flex items have flex-shrink 2 and 4 in a debate layout.

options.text: The item with shrink 2 shrinks more
The item with shrink 4 shrinks more

questions.explanation: Higher flex-shrink means the item gives up more space when shrinking. The item with shrink 4 shrinks more.

questions.topic: A label and the control it describes
questions.stem: A label wraps an input in a debate form without for.

options.text: The association is lost without for
The input is ignored by assistive tech
The association is created by wrapping

questions.explanation: Wrapping creates an implicit association even without for. The label remains meaningful.

questions.topic: Where a required field is enforced
questions.learningObjective: Identify bypass risk of client validation
questions.stem: A debate form relies on required for validation.
questions.explanation: Client-side validation can be bypassed by modifying requests. Server validation is still required.

questions.topic: Tabs and spaces in source and in a preserved listing
questions.learningObjective: Predict rendered output of mixed whitespace
questions.stem: A paragraph contains spaces, tabs, and newlines mixed together.

options.text: The run is kept exactly as written
Only spaces survive and others vanish
options.misconception: thinks tabs and newlines are removed

options.text: The whole run collapses to a single space

questions.explanation: All white space characters collapse to a single space in normal flow. The source mix does not affect the rendered gap.

questions.topic: Why the initial box-sizing surprises people
questions.stem: A content-box element has width 100px, padding 5px, and border 1px.

answer.exemplar: The outer width is 112px because content-box adds both paddings and both borders: 100 + 5 + 5 + 1 + 1 equals 112.

questions.explanation: Content-box excludes padding and border from the declared width, so each side adds to the total. The box ends wider than 100px.
questions.hint: Add both sides of padding and border.

questions.topic: Which flex property works along the line and which across it
questions.learningObjective: Identify the main axis distribution property
questions.stem: A flex container needs space distributed along the main axis.
questions.explanation: justify-content distributes space along the main axis. align-content and align-items work on the cross axis.

questions.topic: What a media query changes and what it leaves alone
questions.learningObjective: Identify media query effect on CSS
questions.stem: A media query is true for a given viewport.

options.text: It enables the matching CSS rules

questions.explanation: When a media query matches, its CSS rules apply. It does not rewrite HTML, change server responses, or reload.

questions.topic: Breaking a tie between equally specific rules
questions.stem: An inline style and a class rule set the same property.

options.text: The class rule wins because it is in a stylesheet
The inline style wins because it has higher specificity

questions.explanation: Inline styles have higher specificity than class rules. The inline value wins.

questions.topic: Weighted shrinking along a flex line

Only the item with shrink 1 shrinks

questions.topic: A label and the control it describes

It improves accessibility for screen readers

questions.explanation: An associated label gives the control an accessible name. It does not style, submit, or disable.

questions.topic: Where a required field is enforced

options.text: The field can be left empty
The field is hidden from users
The field must be filled before submission

questions.explanation: required makes the field mandatory for form submission. It does not hide or disable the field.
